extracted.intended_audience: AI/ML researchers and developers (DARPA proposers, defense-research community) interested in lifelong learning systems
extracted.subtask_description: Research and development of AI/ML systems that learn continuously during execution, improve expertise on the fly, transfer prior skills to new situations without forgetting, and operate safely in unpredictable, dynamic DoD-relevant environments. Work spans system/component engineering and translation of biological learning mechanisms into computational architectures and algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous learning during execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that can learn continuously during execution and become increasingly expert while performing tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes online/in-task learning (learning while deployed), rather than only offline training. Proposals should demonstrate mechanisms by which a system updates and refines behavior during task execution to improve performance over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement of expertise on the fly
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems should 'become increasingly expert while performing tasks.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expected behavior is measurable improvement in task proficiency during operation. Evaluation might track performance trajectories over continued deployment or exposure to task instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer and application of prior skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to apply previous skills and knowledge to new situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems should generalize prior learning to novel contexts without requiring full retraining; demonstrations should show effective reuse/adaptation of learned representations or policies across tasks or domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: No forgetting (retain prior learning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply previous skills and knowledge to new situations - without forgetting previous learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses catastrophic forgetting; solutions should preserve earlier capabilities while acquiring new ones. Evaluation should include retention tests showing maintained performance on prior tasks after learning new tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety limits and innate system constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems are subject to safety limits and should 'incorporate innate system limits' to enhance safety in automated assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs must include mechanisms to bound behavior, enforce safety constraints, and prevent unsafe adaptation. Proposals should describe how safety is preserved during continuous learning and adaptation, including fail-safes, verification, or certifiable limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptivity and rapid reaction in unpredictable/dynamic environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to react quickly and adapt to dynamic, unpredictable circumstances—particularly important for DoD applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems should be evaluated in scenarios with distribution shifts, novel events, or time-critical demands, showing fast adaptation and robust decision-making under uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of complete systems and components (Technical Area 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentrates on the development of complete systems and their components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should address system-level integration as well as component design (algorithms, architectures, sensors, actuators, etc.). Demonstrations of end-to-end systems or interoperable components are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of biological learning mechanisms (Technical Area 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring together researchers to explore biological mechanisms that underlie learning, which will be translated into a new generation of computational architectures, mechanisms, and algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicits biologically inspired approaches: identify biological principles, map them to computational constructs, and demonstrate how those constructs enable lifelong learning properties. Interdisciplinary work (neuroscience + ML) is encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation of novel methodologies, architectures, and algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Discoveries are expected to 'generate new methodologies that will allow AI systems to learn and improve during tasks' and to 'apply previous skills and knowledge to new situations, incorporate innate system limits, and enhance safety.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should produce new, reproducible methods or architectural paradigms that concretely enable the stated lifelong-learning, transfer, retention, and safety properties. Evaluation should highlight novelty, practicality, and potential for DoD-relevant deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on DoD-relevance and operational utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Address limitations of current AI for DoD applications where situations are unpredictable and the ability to react quickly and adapt is critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should contextualize research within defense-relevant use-cases, demonstrate operational utility, and consider constraints (real-time operation, resource limits, adversarial conditions) relevant to DoD deployment.
